title: Why Was Purple the Color of Kings?

fin.big: Simplified illustrations. Facts checked against museum sources.
fin.small: Sources: Science History Institute, William Henry Perkin biography; Science and Industry Museum (UK), World's first synthetic dye

parts: Purple was the color of emperors. Then a teenager brewed a new purple by mistake.
Stay to hear what he was really trying to make.
For centuries, the best purple came from sea snails.
It took thousands, so emperors and the very rich wore it.
In eighteen fifty six, an eighteen year old chemist ran a test over Easter.
He was not after a color. He wanted quinine, the malaria medicine from tree bark.
The test failed and left a black mess. But that mess hid a surprise.
He cleaned it with alcohol, and the liquid turned a deep purple.
It dyed silk. He named the color mauve.
It was the first synthetic dye to sell. A year later, he had a factory.
Made from coal tar, not snails.
Our reading: a failed cure made purple common. Follow for tomorrow's mystery.
